metadata.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List

problem_summary.summary: Remove the node that is n positions from the end of a singly linked list and return the possibly changed head.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: non-null ListNode head and valid n. Return the remaining ListNode head. The judge supplies ListNode { int val; ListNode next; }.

brute_force.explanation: Count the nodes, then use a dummy node and walk to the predecessor of the target at index length - n before bypassing it.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A node at zero-based index length - n is exactly n nodes from the end. The dummy also gives the head a predecessor when that target is the first node.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — one pass counts nodes and another locates the predecessor.

optimized.explanation: Advance fast n links from a dummy node, then move fast and slow together until fast reaches the last node. Slow then precedes the target.
optimized.correctness_idea: The fixed n-link gap means slow is n nodes behind fast. When fast reaches the end, slow is immediately before the node n positions from the end; bypassing slow.next removes exactly that node.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — both pointers make at most one traversal.

steps.condition: Advance fast exactly n links from dummy.
steps.action: Keep slow at dummy while fast moves two nodes.

steps.event: Move both pointers until fast is last.
steps.condition: fast.next is null after the loop.
steps.action: The gap places slow immediately before target node 6.

edge_cases.handling: The dummy is the predecessor, so the head is removed.
The sole node is bypassed and null is returned.
The final node is bypassed from its predecessor.
